title: Solar-Powered Irrigation Scheme — Dokolo District
summary: Deployment of a 15 kW solar water pumping system irrigating 120 acres of rice paddies for 340 smallholder farmers in Dokolo District, Northern Uganda.
description: This project introduced a solar-powered irrigation system in Dokolo District to reduce dependence on rain-fed agriculture among smallholder rice farmers. The system uses a 15 kW solar array to power submersible pumps drawing water from the River Okole into a distribution network covering 120 acres. The project supports 340 farmers — of whom 58% are women — with guaranteed water supply across two growing seasons per year. Farmer groups received training on system operation, maintenance, and cost-recovery mechanisms. A water user association was established to manage the infrastructure on a sustainable basis. The project has contributed to a 40% increase in total rice output and improved incomes in the target communities.
locationNote: River Okole irrigation command area, Dokolo District
outcomes: 340 farmers with year-round irrigation access; 40% increase in rice yields; 58% female participation; water user association established and operational.
